source_text: Ceterum cum res aliqua contra opinionem omnium eo sermone inducitur, in cuius sono habet omne praesidium, graviter peccatur, si proprio eius nomine ad manum posito emendicata abusivi appellatione signetur. Cum ergo de fetibus sermo est, quoniam nullus dubitat, quin natus quisque duos habeat parentes, nec hoc astipulatione indiget, non incommodabit intellectui, si dicam ex uno illum esse generatum; neminem quippe sermo meus adeo permovebit, ut putet illum nasci aut sine patre aut sine matre potuisse.
pass_a_gloss: For the rest, when some thing against the opinion of all is introduced by that speech in whose sound it has every defense, it is gravely sinned if, its proper name placed at hand, it is signed by a begged appellation of the abusive. When therefore speech is about fetuses, since no one doubts that each one born has two parents, and this does not need corroboration, it will not inconvenience understanding if I say he was generated from one; for my speech will move no one so far that he think that one could have been born either without a father or without a mother.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But when something contrary to everyone’s opinion is introduced by an expression whose sound provides its whole support, a serious error is committed if its proper name is readily available but it is labeled with a borrowed, inexact term. When we are speaking of offspring, no one doubts that every person born has two parents, and this needs no corroboration. It will therefore not obstruct understanding if I say that someone was born from one person: my words will not so unsettle anyone that they think he could have been born without either a father or a mother.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
